newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow bounce boosts Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow bounce boosts Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market followed Wall Street higher at the open on Monday, investors taking heart from the Dow rebound and a dip in the U.S. long bond yield after U.S. August payroll data calmed nervous investors.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index climbed 16.7 points to 2,253.7.
The September share price index futures rose 23 points to 2,253, a 0.7 point discount to the underlying index.
"The figures in the U.S. have made some people happier there and that has followed through to our market," said a Sydney broker.
Overall sentiment looked reasonably firm, said the broker, although volumes remained steady rather than impressive.
"It's looking strong so far and overall I think it's looking for reasons to go ahead. Volumes are okay but nothing spectacular," he said.
Featuring early was Newcrest Mining, whose shares found some impetus following the News South Wales government's approval of its A$440 million (US$352.4 million) Cadia Hill copper/gold mine.
Continuing their record breaking run from Friday, QBE Insurance shares jumped ahead again as investors digested its U.K. acquisition announced last week.
Profits continued with oil and gas major Santos posting a sharply higher half year net profit of A$88.6 million and seeing its shares a little firmer.

Shares in radio group Austereo firmed after it reported a higher full year net profit of A$36.46 million, while leisure group Amalgamated Holdings reported a slightly lower full year net profit of A$38.04 million. Its shares were higher, albeit on thin volume.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of four to one, while about 39 perce nt of stocks traded remained steady.
